Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data show about 44,800 Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 47,200 by 2034, a net increase of about 2,400 jobs, with about 3,500 openings per year. The 2026 median annual wage is about $96,700 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary, but it will reshape their workflows. Tools take over repetitive and structured work, while teachers focus on judgment, accountability, explanation, and original research. Formulaic instruction faces pressure, while educators who connect theory to real systems and guide students become more valuable.
